How does moving a card flow through this codebase?

Long image

A

Answer

A drop updates the screen first, then commits to PostgreSQL in one board-locked transaction, and only then fans the change out over SSE. The browser never sends a final position: the server re-derives it from the neighbours you dropped between.

  1. The browser applies an optimistic move before the request leaves.1
  2. The route handler authenticates, rate-limits and validates the drop, then calls cardService.move.2
  3. mutate locks the board, writes the card and its activity row in one transaction, and publishes only after commit.3
  4. Every open board receives card.moved over SSE and re-applies it to the TanStack Query cache.4

Applies toMove one card on a shared boardNext.js App RouterPostgreSQL

1

What are the moving parts?

Diagram structure
  • Board UI ui
  • Query cache cache
  • Route handler api
  • Card service svc
  • PostgreSQL db
  • Event bus bus
  • SSE stream sse
  • Other sessions peers
  • ui → cache · optimistic move
  • cache → api · PATCH /move
  • api → svc · validated input
  • svc → db · locked transaction
  • svc → bus · after commit
  • bus → sse · publish event
  • sse → peers · card.moved

The request path is one direction: UI to cache, cache to route handler, handler to service, service to the database. The event path branches after commit, so a slow reader never holds the transaction open.

2

What happens on drop, step by step?

Diagram structure
  • Browser UI ui
  • Query cache cache
  • Route handler api
  • Card service svc
  • PostgreSQL db
  • Event bus bus
  • SSE stream sse
  • Other sessions peers
  • ui → cache · prepare and apply optimistic move
  • cache → api · PATCH /api/cards/:id/move
  • api → svc · validate, then cardService.move
  • svc → db · lock board, read neighbours
  • svc → db · UPDATE position, INSERT activity
  • db → svc · committed row
  • svc → bus · publish card.moved
  • svc → api · Card DTO
  • api → cache · 200 JSON
  • cache → ui · reconcile, clear pending
  • bus → sse · card.moved event
  • sse → peers · event: card.moved
  1. Browser drag end ↗

    drag-board.tsx calls useMoveCard, which runs commitCardMove. The cache gets the optimistic position before the fetch starts.

  2. PATCH /api/cards/:id/move ↗

    requireUser verifies the session cookie and applies a 120 writes per minute limit. cardMoveSchema parses the drop.

  3. Lock and write ↗

    mutate locks the board row, computes the fractional key from previousId and nextId, updates the card and writes CARD_MOVED activity.

  4. After commit ↗

    The event is published only after the transaction resolves. A publish failure is logged, not returned.

  5. SSE to peers ↗

    The stream writes event: card.moved frames and a heartbeat every 15 seconds. Peers apply the event to their cache.

3

Why is the drop optimistic, and how does it recover?

The screen must not wait for a round trip. The client cancels in-flight board queries, snapshots the card's original column and position, then applies the new slot. If the request fails, it restores that snapshot before showing the error.

SituationWhat the client does
Server acceptsKeeps the optimistic card, then reconciles with the returned DTO
409, 404 or 5xxReverts the snapshot and refetches the board
Other 4xxReverts the snapshot only

Concurrent moves can still lose the slot

If another move fills the same gap first, positionInGap appends behind it. If the anchors no longer line up, the service retries the ordering transaction up to three times, then returns 409 STALE_ORDER. The client reverts and refetches.

4

What does the server trust from the browser?

Very little. The request carries a target column and the two neighbour IDs, not an absolute position. The service reads the current siblings, checks the gap is still valid, and generates a fractional key with generateKeyBetween.

Sent by the client
columnId, previousId, nextId
Ignored by the server
any absolute position
Recomputed by
positionInGap from neighbour positions
Ordering retry
up to 3 attempts on a repository conflict
Hard failure
409 STALE_ORDER, then revert and refetch
Write identity
X-Client-Id is stored as originClientId on the event
